title: The Grandfather Paradox
summary: If you travelled back in time and prevented your grandparents from meeting, you would never be born, so you could never travel back to prevent it. The puzzle appears in René Barjavel's novel Le Voyageur imprudent (1943) and became a standard objection to the very possibility of time travel. In "The Paradoxes of Time Travel" (1976), David Lewis argued that the traveller Tim can, in one sense, kill his grandfather, but will not: he will fail for some commonplace reason, because the past already happened the way it did.
citations: David Lewis, "The Paradoxes of Time Travel," American Philosophical Quarterly 13 (1976): 145–152
